Package org.aristonis.diwan.database.eloquent.relations

package org.aristonis.diwan.database.eloquent.relations
Eloquent relations: the relation types a model declares, their name map, and their exceptions.

A model declares each relation as a typed method that builds it, and lists the methods in a RelationMap returned from relations(), the way casts() lists casts: 


 public final class Post extends Model {
     public static final ModelQuery<Post> query = ModelQuery.of(Post.class, Post::new);

     public HasMany<Comment> comments() {
         return hasMany(Comment.class);
     }

     protected RelationMap<Post> relations() {
         return RelationMap.of(Post.class).add("comments", Post::comments);
     }
 }

hasOne and hasMany relations can link each child back to its parent with chaperone() or chaperone(name). Without a name the inverse is guessed from the foreign key, the parent's foreign key, the parent's class name, owner and, for a self relation, parent. R8 renames classes on Android, so pass the name there.

This package holds the public relation types, the name map and factory, the three relation exceptions, and the package-private machinery behind eager loading, existence queries, relation aggregates and their load* form, touching owners and inverse linking. It does not hold relation state on a model or the builder's with and has methods; those stay in org.aristonis.diwan.database.eloquent. The cycle between the two packages is accepted, as it is for casts. Neither package reaches the other's package-private members except through org.aristonis.diwan.database.eloquent.internal, which is not API.

BelongsToMany is the many-to-many kind, alongside hasOne, hasMany and belongsTo. Its read side covers lazy, eager and existence queries, relation aggregates, finders, iteration and pages, and the pivot configuration with the wherePivot family. Each related row carries its joining row as a Pivot, a model of its own. The write side of belongsToMany is in this package too: attach, detach, sync, toggle and the saves of related models that write the joining rows. It sits in layers that extend the read side.

    Description
    BelongsTo<R extends Model>
    The inverse of a has-one or has-many relation: the model this relation is built on, the child, holds the foreign key, and it points at a column of the related owner, such as a post's author.
    BelongsToMany<R extends Model>
    A many-to-many relation through a pivot table, such as a user's roles through role_user: Laravel's BelongsToMany.
    HasMany<R extends Model>
    A one-to-many relation whose related rows hold the key, such as a post's comments: Laravel's HasMany.
    HasManyThrough<R extends Model>
    A has-many-through relation: the far parent has many related rows through an intermediate model, such as a country with many posts through its users.
    HasOne<R extends Model>
    A one-to-one relation whose related row holds the key, such as a user's profile: Laravel's HasOne.
    HasOneOrMany<R extends Model,S extends HasOneOrMany<R,S>>
    A relation whose related rows hold the key: the related table has a foreign key column that points at a column of the parent, its local key.
    HasOneOrManyThrough<R extends Model,S extends HasOneOrManyThrough<R,S>>
    A relation that reaches the related rows through an intermediate table: the far parent owns through rows, and each through row owns related rows.
    HasOneThrough<R extends Model>
    A one-to-one relation that reaches the related row through an intermediate model, such as a mechanic's owner through the car: Laravel's HasOneThrough.
    MorphEagerOptions
    The per-class options of an eager loaded MorphTo: which relations and relation counts to load on the owners of one model class, and a constraint for that class's query.
    MorphMany<R extends Model>
    A polymorphic one-to-many relation, such as a post's comments: Laravel's MorphMany.
    MorphMap
    The global map between morph aliases and model classes, a port of Laravel's Relation::morphMap, enforceMorphMap and requireMorphMap.
    MorphOne<R extends Model>
    A polymorphic one-to-one relation, such as a post's image: Laravel's MorphOne.
    MorphOneOrMany<R extends Model,S extends MorphOneOrMany<R,S>>
    A polymorphic has-one or has-many: the related rows hold the parent's key in an id column and the parent's morph class in a type column.
    MorphPivot
    A row of a morph-to-many join table: a Pivot that also knows the type column and the type value of the relation that built it, such as taggables.taggable_type and Post.
    MorphTo<R extends Model>
    The inverse of a morph-one or morph-many relation: the model this relation is built on, the child, holds a type column and an id column, and together they point at an owner of any model class, such as a comment's post or video.
    MorphToMany<R extends Model>
    A polymorphic many-to-many relation, such as the tags of a post or a video: Laravel's MorphToMany.
    Pivot
    A row of a belongsToMany join table, as a model: the pivot columns of a related model, such as role_user.status for one of a user's roles.
    Relation<R extends Model,S extends Relation<R,S>>
    A relation between a parent model and the related model class: Laravel's Eloquent Relation, with HasOne, HasMany and BelongsTo as its kinds.
    RelationFactory<M extends Model>
    Builds one relation of a model; usually a method reference to the model's relation method, such as Post::comments.
    RelationMap<M extends Model>
    The relations a model class can load by name, in the order they were added; what a model returns from relations().
    SyncResult
    What a sync or toggle changed in a join table: the related keys attached, detached and updated.
